Article Title: Jamie Dimon warns, as AI companies ‘boast’ their Agents can do a lot including making payments for customers; says: Don’t allow that as they will …
Article Text:
Jamie Dimon highlights dangers of rogue consumer AI agents

AI is moving ‘more like a Tsunami’

As artificial intelligence (AI) developers boast that autonomous agents can manage personal errands, book travel, and even execute purchases, JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is urging consumers and financial institutions not to allow AI agents to handle direct banking payments. Speaking at The Economic Club of Chicago this week, Dimon cautioned that authorising a software agent to execute payments requires handing over sensitive banking codes and if done, it is effectively inviting unvetted algorithms deep inside personal accounts with no promise that it will protect your best interests.“That means they are in your bank and you’re assuming they’re going to act properly on your behalf and they may not,” Dimon said, warning that autonomous agents could carry out actions that prove “treacherous” for financial institutions.Dimon’s comments arrive amid rapid commercial adoption of consumer-facing AI agents that are capable of managing personal calendars, drafting emails and coordinating travel bookings. The JPMorgan chief previously sounded alarms during the bank’s third-quarter earnings call, warning that the financial system could soon contend with thousands of rogue agents. Dimon noted that autonomous tools may execute round-the-clock cyber intrusions or trigger vulnerabilities if granted access to consumer accounts.Despite the warnings, JPMorgan is advancing its own controlled implementations. Company CFO Jeremy Barnum confirmed that the lender’s proprietary Smart Cash tool, which has been built to help clients oversee and balance liquidity across multiple accounts, is currently undergoing an early-stage pilot. JPMorgan has used AI internally since 2012 across functions including risk assessment, fraud prevention, marketing, credit underwriting, and customer support.Drawing historical parallels, Dimon compared the rapid rise of AI to the Industrial Revolution, but noted that modern computing shifts are occurring at high speeds. Calling the rapid spread of the technology “more like a tsunami” that cannot be stopped, Dimon argued that public institutions and corporate leaders must move quickly to contain digital fallout: “You can’t stop it. You just have to, like, manage the hell out of it. ”With open-source releases and systems originating worldwide, Dimon emphasised that global governments cannot simply halt model proliferation. The technology’s acceleration is backed by massive capital flows, with tech giants Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta planning more than $700 billion in capital expenditures this year, primarily dedicated to AI infrastructure.Recently, JP Morgan Chase, Citi Bank and Bank of America ‘banned’ AI agents from logging into customer accounts and moving money. They fear that the software could initiate uncontrolled cash movements and erode vital deposit bases.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warns of dangers of rogue consumer AI agents. Warns that authorising a software agent to execute payments requires handing over sensitive banking codes. If done, it is effectively inviting unvetted algorithms deep inside personal accounts with no promise that it will protect your best interests.

Article Title: Two researchers may have just proved connected cars can be unlocked, started from thousands of miles away
Article Text:
Disclaimer: Its an AI-generated image used for representative purpose only

Inside the connected-car security flaws

In early 2026, two security researchers demonstrated that hackers could remotely unlock the doors and start the engines of internet-connected cars from anywhere in the world. Working together, white-hat hackers Shubham Shah and Sam Curry breached the backend connectivity systems of two major automakers. Beyond taking remote control of the vehicles, the flaws also exposed sensitive customer data, including personal information, vehicle locations, mileage, fuel levels, driving range, and whether the doors were locked or unlocked.In a note shared earlier this month, the duo said that both automakers have since patched the vulnerabilities, which stemmed from basic security oversights in the server APIs powering their mobile apps. Shah and Curry have not publicly named either company. However, they confirmed that the first automaker’s vulnerabilities affected vehicles in the US, while the second automaker’s flaws left cars open to remote unlocking across the US, Canada and Australia.While the researchers kept the brands anonymous, visual clues in their demonstration video, suggesting the second automaker may be Toyota, as per a report by Tom’s Hardware.According to the researchers’ write-ups, both companies relied on ForgeRock for user authentication and authorisation. Aside from one minor exception, the breaches weren't caused by ForgeRock itself but rather by how poorly the automakers implemented it. In a detailed breakdown of the second automaker’s Australian infrastructure, Shah explained how the duo gained access.After spending a couple of weeks studying how the automaker used ForgeRock, the researchers realised the easiest way was to generate their own access tokens for any user account. The pair used GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra to brute-force hidden URL paths. They eventually uncovered an unprotected endpoint that let them overwrite any user's password.The final hurdle was multi-factor authentication (MFA), which turned out to be misconfigured. In the Australian system, users could simply skip the MFA step altogether. By shuffling tokens between the mobile app and the backend endpoints, Shah and Curry were able to mint valid access tokens, fully impersonate any customer and send a "door-unlock" API request – promptly opening the test vehicle.
Article Summary: Security researchers demonstrated that hackers could remotely unlock the doors and start the engines of internet-connected cars from anywhere in the world. White-hat hackers Shubham Shah and Sam Curry breached the backend connectivity systems of two major automakers. The flaws also exposed sensitive customer data, including personal information, vehicle locations, mileage, fuel levels, driving range, and whether the doors were locked or unlocked.

Article Title: Meta’s chief strategy officer Dave Wehner is leaving the company for four-year-old AI startup; sends 'right mission' message; says: I have become increasingly ...
Article Text:
From Meta veteran to AI challenger

Fireworks eyes its next phase of growth

AI boom draws senior executives

AI race intensifies

Read Meta chief strategy officer Dave Wehner’s complete post here

Wehner's move underscores the growing pull of the AI industry as startups compete with larger rivals such as OpenAI, Anthropic and major cloud providers.

With fresh capital, rising valuations and growing enterprise demand for AI infrastructure, companies like Fireworks are increasingly attracting experienced leaders who see artificial intelligence as the next major technology platform.

Read Meta chief strategy officer Dave Wehner’s complete post here

I announced earlier this week that I am leaving Meta. I am deeply grateful to Mark Zuckerberg for showing what a truly founder-led company can achieve.

I am incredibly optimistic for Meta’s future.

At Meta, I was able to witness the most exciting opportunities in enterprise AI. That’s why today, I’m announcing that I will be joining Fireworks as CFO. I am thrilled to be joining a founder-led growth company where I can roll up my sleeves and put my experience to work.

Fireworks has the right mission for the moment. Companies will use AI to build on what makes them distinctive: their data and expertise.

Specialized intelligence gives them a way to capture those advantages and own their “alpha.” Open models offer price points that allow the technology to have the greatest impact. Fireworks is building the platform to make all of this possible.

I’ve known and respected Lin

for a long time. As I’ve spent more time with her and the people at Fireworks, I’ve become increasingly bullish on what they are building. There’s a remarkable depth of technical talent here, coupled with a very practical focus on what customers need.

I see AI as the most consequential technology shift of my lifetime. I’m excited to get to work and help build a business at the center of it.

Dave Wehner, Meta’s chief strategy officer and former chief financial officer, is leaving the social media giant to join fast-growing AI startup Lin Qiao-led Fireworks as its new CFO, marking another high-profile move from Big Tech into the artificial intelligence sector. Wehner announced the move in a post on X, saying he had become increasingly convinced of the opportunity ahead for the four-year-old startup. “Fireworks has the right mission for the moment,” he wrote. “I’ve become increasingly bullish on what they are building. There’s a remarkable depth of technical talent here, coupled with a very practical focus on what customers need.” Fireworks, which provides AI inference and model-training services built around open-source AI models, was valued at $17.5 billion in a Series D funding round in July.Wehner joined Meta, then known as Facebook, in 2012 and served as the company’s chief financial officer from 2014 to 2022 before taking on the role of chief strategy officer. During his tenure, he helped steer the company through a period of rapid growth, expanding advertising revenues and major bets on new technologies. In a statement to CNBC, Meta COO Javier Olivan praised Wehner's contributions, saying he helped guide the company through “tremendous growth and complexity” over the past 14 years while bringing disciplined thinking to some of its most important strategic decisions.At Fireworks, Wehner will oversee the company's finances and operations as it looks to scale further in the increasingly competitive AI market. CEO Lin Qiao said Wehner's experience would help the company as it enters its next stage of expansion.Founded in 2022 by former Meta and Google employees, Fireworks allows developers and businesses to customise, train and run open AI models. The company counts investors such as Nvidia and Sequoia Capital among its backers and has reportedly held early discussions for another funding round that could value the startup between $30 billion and $40 billion.“Dave told me he wanted to get back to a smaller company where he could build toward a big impact again,” Qiao wrote in a LinkedIn post. “He sees AI as the defining technology shift of his lifetime and wants to help shape what comes next.”Wehner's departure comes as venture-backed AI companies continue to attract seasoned executives from some of the world's largest technology firms. While Fireworks remains significantly smaller than Meta, which had a market capitalisation of about $1.56 trillion at Friday's close, the startup is positioning itself as a key player in the market for open AI models.The company has also faced challenges associated with rapid growth. In October, Fireworks disclosed a security incident involving unauthorised use of internal credentials that allowed limited access to environment variables used in evaluation jobs within a small number of customer accounts. The company said its investigation found no evidence of unauthorised access to customer models, datasets, training data, personal information or inference traffic.Wehner's move underscores the growing pull of the AI industry as startups compete with larger rivals such as OpenAI, Anthropic and major cloud providers. With fresh capital, rising valuations and growing enterprise demand for AI infrastructure, companies like Fireworks are increasingly attracting experienced leaders who see artificial intelligence as the next major technology platform.
Article Summary: Dave Wehner, Meta’s chief strategy officer and former chief financial officer, is leaving the social media giant to join fast-growing AI startup Fireworks. Wehner announced the move in a post on X, saying he had become increasingly convinced of the opportunity ahead for the four-year-old startup. Fireworks provides AI inference and model-training services built around open-source AI models.

Article Title: Silicon Valley’s call to speed up AI to fight China may no longer work; as in group chats and phone calls, left-leaning donors and advisers are planning to change …
Article Text:
‘Tech executives trading AI speed for community concessions’

Tech giants have begun offering olive branches

For the first two years of President Donald Trump’s second term, Silicon Valley’s most powerful executives made a public show of loyalty. Top CEOs sat on the dais at Trump’s inauguration and showered the administration with gifts and donations, including money for the White House ballroom. In return, they got access, deregulation and a green light for rapid AI expansion, a report has said, adding that right-leaning figures like Elon Musk and venture capitalist David Sacks took formal roles in the government. Now, after Democrats swept races across the country in midterms last week – driven in large part by voter anger over data centers and artificial intelligence – a different faction of the tech world is quietly organising a course correction.Citing eight strategists, executives and investors familiar with the talks, a report by The Washington Post claims that in private group chats and phone calls, left-leaning donors and advisers are working to take control of the industry’s agenda away from Trump-aligned tech leaders. The report, however, noted that it is still too early to know if this group will sway the broader tech sector as Congress changes hands.To win back public trust, these left-leaning voices are said to be floating ideas that would have been unthinkable in Silicon Valley until recently. The proposals include slowing down or pausing data center construction, pouring billions of dollars into local schools and job training, requiring union labor at data centers and protecting residents from higher electricity bills.Some industry figures have already started making this case publicly. In a September blog post, investor Reid Hoffman urged the tech sector to offer Americans a clear economic pitch, writing that “the public deserves the benefits of AI as soon as there are any, not a generation from now after a hard transition.”OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, echoed that sentiment in an interview, saying companies will need to move “beyond the table stakes of paying for energy, preserving water, addressing noise and generating tax revenue.” Instead, he said, tech firms must let local communities “increasingly exercise more of a direct say” over where corporate money goes.“Communities have every right to use their control over these projects so as to ensure that they are getting meaningful benefits,” Lehane added.Even before any new laws are passed, public pressure and shifting politics are reportedly forcing tech companies to offer bigger concessions to the towns hosting their data centers.For example, Google and Microsoft recently announced they will stop forcing government officials to sign controversial nondisclosure agreements that kept data center plans hidden from the public. Moreover, Amazon reportedly pledged to share more details about how much water and energy its data centers consume.Both Meta and Amazon recently committed $1 billion each to host communities for local investments like schools and job training. On Saturday, data center firm CoreWeave also moved to build bridges with newly elected Democrats, writing to congratulate Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who campaigned on restricting data centers.“As you have noted, communities should have a voice, households should not be left paying for new infrastructure and development should protect local water, power, and quality of life. We strongly support those principles,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator wrote.Meanwhile, some of them are breaking with the Trump-aligned crowd as much of the pushback from the left is aimed directly at the right-wing tech leaders who championed the current approach. Critics inside the industry blame figures like former AI czar David Sacks, investor Marc Andreessen and their online supporters as well as those tech leaders who issued doomsday AI warnings for sparking the public backlash.“They won an election having supported Trump thinking we can do whatever we want, and that was wrong,” one of the people familiar with the discussions said, The Washington Post says. Sacks has previously blamed the public's resistance on tech factions that spent years issuing apocalyptic warnings about AI.Following the midterm defeats, the normally vocal pro-Trump wing of Silicon Valley went noticeably quiet. On the November 8 episode of the “All-In” podcast some hosts sounded unusually reflective.“I thought top-down economics can still work. I thought that when you had asset owners building assets and investing in the economy, these things can get to everybody else. It’s clearly not happening. It’s not true,” said tech investor Chamath Palihapitiya, who fundraised for Trump.Still, Trump’s tech allies retain influence inside the White House, and they are already gearing up for a fight with the incoming Congress. On the same podcast, Sacks argued that Democrats would use AI rules to expand government control: "I believe that Democrats want to create a surveillance and censorship state that’s turbocharged by super intelligence."
Article Summary: Tech giants have begun offering olive branches to towns hosting their data centers. Left-leaning donors and advisers are working to take control of the industry's agenda away from Trump-aligned tech leaders. Critics inside the industry blame figures like former AI czar David Sacks, investor Marc Andreessen and their online supporters for sparking the public backlash.

Article Title: Government has a ‘critical’ warning for Google Chrome users: Here’s what you should do
Article Text:
Government has a ‘critical’ warning for Google Chrome users: Here’s what you should do

What the vulnerability means for Google Chrome users

What should Google Chrome users do

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued a warning for Google Chrome, asking users to update their browser immediately. In an advisory rated ‘critical’, the cyber agency said multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in Google Chrome which could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code, bypass security restrictions, or cause denial of service (Dos) conditions on the targeted system. The versions impacted by these vulnerabilities include Google Chrome versions prior to 157.0.8103.50 and Google Chrome Extended Stable versions prior to 156.0.8078.96.In the advisory, the CERT-In says that all Google Chrome users are at high “risk of arbitrary code execution and compromise of affected systems”.“These vulnerabilities exist in Google Chrome due to use after free in XML, type confusion in V8, out-of-bounds write in GPU, incorrect authorization in FileSystem, buffer overflow in Compositing, and uninitialized resource bugs in WebGL and GPU,” the agency said.CERT-In says that the vulnerability in Google Chrome can allow a remote attacker to persuade a victim to visit a specially crafted webpage. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code, bypass security restrictions, or cause denial of service (DoS) conditions on the targeted system.“This vulnerability (CVE-2026-125350) is being actively exploited in the wild.Users are strongly advised to apply the latest patches immediately,” the agency said.Google Chrome users are advised to apply appropriate updates. Google has released a stable channel update for desktop users. Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild, the tech giant said adding “The Stable channel has been updated to 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Mac and 157.0.8103.50 to Linux which will roll out over the coming days/weeks”.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued a warning for Google Chrome, asking users to update their browser immediately. In an advisory rated ‘critical’, the cyber agency said multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in Google Chrome. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code.

Article Title: Days after donating $10 million to Nashville Symphony, Larry Ellison’s Oracle breaks ground on new 78-acre headquarters in Tennessee; aims to create thousands of high-quality jobs
Article Text:
Days after donating $10 million to Nashville Symphony, Larry Ellison’s Oracle breaks ground on new 78-acre headquarters in Tennessee; aims to create thousands of high-quality jobs

Oracle breaks ground on 70-acre Nashville headquarters

Oracle plans $175 million for public infrastructure

Oracle’s $10 million Nashville Symphony commitment

A month after committing $10 million to help keep the Nashville Symphony afloat during a financial crisis, Oracle has broken ground on its future global headquarters in Nashville, Tennessee. The November 11 ceremony marks another major step in the tech giant’s growing investment in the city, with plans for a sprawling riverfront campus expected to create thousands of high-quality jobs. The development, it said, will strengthen Oracle’s presence in a city increasingly positioning itself as a hub for technology and healthcare, while also bringing new public infrastructure, green spaces, retail and hospitality facilities to Nashville’s East Bank.Oracle CEOs Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia joined Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, Nashville Mayor Freddie O’Connell, Governor-elect Marsha Blackburn and other state and local leaders for the groundbreaking ceremony. The planned campus will span approximately 78 acres in Nashville’s East Bank, transforming a former industrial site into a new headquarters for Oracle’s growing cloud, AI and healthcare technology operations.The first buildings are expected to open in 2030. The development will include retail spaces, a 120-room Nobu hotel and restaurant, and more than 1,900 trees. Oracle is also targeting LEED Gold certification across the campus.The company said it has already recruited engineering and technical talent locally and expects hiring to accelerate over the coming years. Its Nashville workforce includes healthcare technology professionals, as well as teams in sales, marketing and other business functions.Beyond the headquarters, Oracle’s investment includes $175 million for public infrastructure improvements. These include a pedestrian bridge across the Cumberland River, a public park, greenway connections and street upgrades.The planned bridge is expected to connect surrounding neighbourhoods with the campus and park, providing new routes for everyday travel and recreation. Nashville Mayor Freddie O’Connell said the development would help make the East Bank more accessible to residents.“Our East Bank should bring us closer together as Nashvillians, serving as a guide for how we build great communities,” said O’Connell.Oracle’s growing investment in Nashville also includes support for local cultural institutions.On October 4, the company announced a $10 million partnership with the Nashville Symphony as the organisation faced a financial emergency. The funding helped the Symphony reinstate its 2026-27 season and bring back full-time staff and orchestra members who were scheduled to be furloughed on October 18.Oracle CEO Clay Magouyrk said the company wanted to help address community needs as it builds its headquarters in the city.“Nashville is a city that understands how music can bring people together,” Magouyrk said. “We are part of this community and understand how important cultural institutions like this are to the residents of Nashville. As Oracle builds its new headquarters on Nashville’s East Bank, we are here to help solve the community’s problems and ensure Nashville remains a vibrant place to live and work for generations to come. ”Oracle has also announced a $1.55 million grant to Trinity Community Commons for renovations to its community hub and dining room, alongside $150,000 in grants to 30 local nonprofits through its employee-directed giving programme.
Article Summary: Oracle breaks ground on new 78-acre headquarters in Tennessee. Plans for a sprawling riverfront campus expected to create thousands of high-quality jobs. The development will include retail spaces, a 120-room Nobu hotel and restaurant, and more than 1,900 trees.

Article Title: Polymarket confirms 'Difficult news' email going viral on social media; say: As we have brought new leadership ...
Article Text:
Company cites reorganisation, leadership changes

Competition from Kalshi intensifies

New executives join Polymarket

Regulatory scrutiny

Prediction market platform Polymarket has confirmed the authenticity of an internal email that surfaced on social media, as the company undergoes a workforce restructuring aimed at positioning itself for its next phase of growth amid intensifying competition from rival Kalshi. According to a Reuters report, the email, which has been circulating on X since last week, informed some contractors that their agreements would be terminated as part of a broader reduction in force. Polymarket confirmed on Wednesday that the screenshot shared online was genuine. "We're reaching out with difficult news. As part of a company-wide reduction in force, we've made the decision to end your contractor agreement with Polymarket effective November 4, 2026," the email stated, according to Reuters.In a statement emailed to Reuters, Polymarket said the changes were part of a broader organisational overhaul following recent leadership appointments. "As we've grown and brought on new leadership, we've reorganized to set the company up for its next phase of growth, which has meant a lot of new hires, changes in personnel and letting some people go," the company said. The New York-based startup did not disclose how much of its workforce was affected.However, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters that more than half of those impacted were contractors.The restructuring at Ploymarket comes as the company is trying to regain momentum against rival Kalshi, which has gained the position of a dominant player in the prediction market segment. As reported by Reuters, Polymarket, once the market leader, now trails Kalshi in monthly trading volume. Kalshi has managed to expand its reach by adding new distribution channels and commercial partnerships including major FIFA World Cup-related deal. The competition between Kalshi and Polymarket further increased after Kalshi announced a $1 billion funding round last month that valued the company at $40 billion.Polymarket named veteran finance executive Warren Jenson as its first chief financial officer in September. It also brought on former Uber executive Travis VanderZanden as chief growth officer this year.Both prediction markets have faced government scrutiny over some marketing and other practices. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is investigating whether Polymarket broke a 2022 enforcement deal in which it promised to bar US users from its main overseas platform, Reuters reported last month, citing people familiar with the matter. Polymarket is based in New York and has an offshore entity registered in Panama.
Article Summary: Prediction market platform Polymarket confirms authenticity of internal email that surfaced on social media. Email informed some contractors that their agreements would be terminated as part of a broader reduction in force. Company cites reorganisation, leadership changes and regulatory scrutiny as reasons for restructuring.

Article Title: Jensen Huang was asked if daughter Madison would succeed him as Nvidia CEO weeks before admitting to his affair; he said: I don’t wish the job on her, they have to...
Article Text:
Will Madison Huang be Nvidia’s next CEO? Jensen Huang answered weeks ago

Jensen Huang hoped Nvidia’s next CEO was already at the company

Madison and Spencer Huang have been rising through Nvidia’s ranks

Nvidia’s board is hunting for Jensen Huang’s replacement without a succession plan

About a month before Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair, the Nvidia CEO was asked a question that now sits at the centre of the company’s biggest crisis: could his daughter, Madison, be the one to take over? “I don’t wish the job on her,” Huang said. If running Nvidia was what she and her brother Spencer wanted, he added, “they have to go earn it.”That answer lands very differently this week. Huang, 63, acknowledged on November 8 that he had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom US intelligence agencies have concluded was spying for China. On November 11, The New York Times reported a second relationship, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal now reports that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust him.The question came in an interview with Bloomberg, filmed about a month ago, which covers Huang’s flat way of running Nvidia, with as few silos as possible, and what comes after him. “I’m really hoping that the next CEO of the company is already at the company,” he said. He described himself as “completely fireable” and said the bar for the job is supposed to be high.“Just as I can be fired, the next CEO has to be hired.”On his children, he chose his words carefully. “It’s really, really hard work; it takes a lot of sacrifice,” he said, adding that a CEO cares for his own family “but I’ve got a whole bunch of other families I’m caring for.”Around the same time, Huang described his dealings with Alice Huang as “completely normal and not unusual.” He has since admitted otherwise.Madison Huang is a senior director of product marketing who works on robotics as well as communications and marketing. Spencer Huang is a director of product management with a leading role in Nvidia’s robotics efforts. Huang’s son-in-law, Nico Caprez, works in business development.Five current and former employees told the NYT that Huang has steadily handed his children more power over the past few years. Their direct access to him has created odd dynamics in meetings, and some customers and suppliers have started cultivating ties with them. Inside the company, that has fed a belief that he is preparing them for the top job.Still, both are director-level in a company where Huang has around 60 direct reports and the final word on every major decision.Nvidia has no public succession plan and no obvious internal candidate. Arm CEO Rene Haas, who worked at Nvidia from 2006 to 2013, has said Huang resisted one, fearing it would create competition among executives. The WSJ notes that Nvidia’s own proxy statement warns it is highly dependent on its longstanding executive team.Recruiter Jeff Christian told the NYT that most Nvidia executives run specific products or technology areas, which makes a stand-in hard to find. Removing Huang, he said, is “almost like trying to fire the owner.” Huang is also Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a 3.56% stake.The board has now brought in outside help. Bloomberg reported on November 11 that directors have been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Huang, and are weighing an interim CEO in the meantime. A month earlier, Huang had said he hoped Nvidia’s next chief was already inside the company.Law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz is leading the board’s investigation, a class-action shareholder lawsuit was filed on November 9, and the Republican leaders of three House committees want Huang at a closed-door briefing this month. Nvidia’s stock is down roughly a third from its early October peak, a loss of more than $1.5 trillion in market value.According to the WSJ, the board planned to meet as soon as November 11 to decide his future, and the NYT reports that the meeting took place. Nvidia declined to comment. When the Times reached Huang by phone about Powell, he said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” and hung up.If the board does move, Huang’s own words from that interview set the terms. He said he could be fired, and that the next CEO has to be hired. By his standard, that applies to Madison and Spencer as much as anyone else at Nvidia.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with an executive at Singapore- based Megaspeed whom US intelligence agencies have concluded was spying for China. On November 11, The New York Times reported a second relationship, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. The Wall Street Journal now reports that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust him.

Article Title: Nvidia Board issues another statement, two days after almost saying not 'firing' CEO Jensen Huang; says …
Article Text:
First statement from Nvidia’s board of directors on CEO Jesen Huang's affair

Read Huang’s email to Nvidia employee

Nvidia’s board of directors said on Tuesday (November 10) that it has hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang and whether company secrets or national security was compromised, after Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, CEO of Singapore-based company MegaSpeed. Alice Hunag has been connected to Chinese intelligence.In the statement, the Nvidia board said, “The independent members of the NVIDIA Board have retained former acting U.S. Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday.” Kim joined the AI chip giant Nvidia in October, and he was previously the chief US prosecutor in Manhattan. Nvidia’s board has 10 independent members, including a former president of Taco Bell, a former Eli Lilly executive and a former vice chairman from Goldman Sachs. Nvidia’s lead independent director and head of corporate governance is Stephen Neal. According to reports, Neal’s experience makes him a likely key figure in the investigation.Also Read| Trump administration aware of plans to oust Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: Report In its first statement on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair, Nvidia’s board on Sunday (November 8) said that it would investigate the allegations that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders. While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate," read the full statement from the board.The allegations on Jensen Huang come as Nvidia has become the center of a trade dispute between China and the US as AI is seen as increasingly critical to US national security. Over the past two years, US government has refused to allow sale of top-end Nvidia chips to China, citing national security concerns as well as to protect America's lead in AI space.Below is the email that Jensen Huang sent to Nvidia employees. Analysts also pointed out that Jensen Huang's two children and son-in-law too are Nvidia employees, which means that the mail 'reaches' out to them to as well.To my colleagues at NVIDIA,I owe my family and all of you an apology.I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy.— Jensen
Article Summary: N Nvidia's board of directors has hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang. Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, CEO of Singapore-based company MegaSpeed. Alice Hunag has been connected to Chinese intelligence. The allegations come as Nvidia has become the center of a trade dispute between China and the US.

Article Title: Google allows users check and correct what Gemini remembers about them; what the new Memory summary feature does and how it works
Article Text:
What does Gemini Memory summary show

How can users check and change it

Who can access the feature

Does removing a memory delete its source chat

Article Title: Microsoft’s AI upscaler now works in handheld mode and hits up to 120fps
Article Text:
Microsoft’s upscaler goes handheld

Ally X owners now have two upscalers to choose from

Microsoft has started rolling out Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR), its AI upscaling tech that competes with Nvidia’s DLSS and AMD’s FSR, to the ROG Xbox Ally X, ROG Xbox Ally X20 and select Copilot+ PCs. The official release removes the preview’s biggest limitation: you no longer have to dock the handheld to use it.Microsoft began testing Auto SR on the Ally X in April, but only for docked play on a bigger screen. The final version works in handheld mode, even on battery. It also supports games running at the Ally’s native 1080p, so you don’t have to lower the in-game resolution first.That comes with a caveat. Microsoft product manager Stefan Bojanic said that at 1080p in handheld mode, “performance may not be as optimal as other configurations.” He added that players should still see sharper visuals, “especially in older games.”The other big addition is a new Performance mode. The preview capped the upscaler at around 60 to 75fps, and that limit still applies to the default Quality mode. Performance mode raises it to 120fps, which should help in fast shooters. Auto SR now also works with Auto HDR, which adds HDR to games that never shipped with it. Both will arrive through Windows updates, so they “may take a little time to reach your device,” Bojanic noted.Last month, AMD brought FSR 4.1 to Ally handhelds with the Z2 Extreme chip, so Ally X and X20 owners already had one upscaling option. Auto SR is built into Windows and is meant for games you already own. It renders a game at a lower resolution, then uses the neural processing unit (NPU) to scale the image up, all on the device. That’s why the base ROG Xbox Ally, which has no NPU, can’t use it. Nvidia’s DLSS doesn’t run natively on any of these handhelds.Auto SR has its own limits too. Games must use DirectX 10 or later and run on x64 or Arm64, which leaves out DirectX 9, Vulkan and OpenGL titles. You turn it on per game from the Display widget in Xbox Game Bar (Win + G), and the game has to be in fullscreen.
Article Summary: Microsoft has started rolling out Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR) to the ROG Xbox Ally X, X20 and select Copilot+ PCs. It works in handheld mode, even on battery. It also supports games running at the Ally’s native 1080p, so you don’t have to lower the in-game resolution first.

Article Title: Cisco adds Anthropic’s Claude Mythos to AI Defense to help companies test their AI agents
Article Text:
Claude Mythos to red team AI agents

Cisco is putting tight limits on how customers use Claude Mythos

Splunk wants companies to see what every AI agent costs and delivers

Cisco is adding Claude Mythos, Anthropic's most capable AI model, to its AI Defense platform. Enterprises can use it to attack their own AI agents before someone else does. The company announced the move at Cisco Live APJC in Melbourne on Tuesday, along with new Splunk tools that track what AI agents cost and whether that spend pays off.Mythos will sit inside AI Defense's adaptive red teaming framework, which security teams use to build custom, multi-step attacks on AI models, apps and agents. Cisco says the model will plan the tests that matter, map attack paths across complex systems and turn each round of results into fresh attack ideas. Every action is logged for audit."You cannot scale what you cannot secure, govern, or observe," said Cisco President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel.Customers won't get open-ended prompt access. They work only through AI Defense's structured interface, and tests run only against systems they have registered, own and authorised. Each engagement is cryptographically tied to a named operator and follows objectives set by a human. It also runs in a time-bound session that can be halted on demand.The caution is deliberate. Cisco notes that frontier models are skilled at crafting attack strategies, and that the same ability is lowering the barrier for attackers.Michael Moore, Cybersecurity Lead at Anthropic, said enterprises want to test their agents thoroughly before putting them into production.The new Tokenomics feature pulls usage data from Amazon Bedrock and Amazon CloudWatch and pairs each agent's cost with graded evaluations of its work. It builds on token-spend tracking introduced at .conf26, which follows spending across coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.Splunk is also offering Eval-G1, small custom models that run evaluations and guardrails at up to 98% lower cost than a commercial LLM, and they respond 2.5 times faster. An Evaluation Tuner lets teams turn agent traces and expert feedback into their own evaluator models.Cisco IQ, used by close to 17,000 customers across more than 22 million devices, will now feed vulnerability data into Splunk and turn exposure findings into ServiceNow problem records.Mythos-powered red teaming arrives soon for select enterprises. Tokenomics enters private preview in December and reaches AWS Marketplace in early 2027. The evaluation models and tuner are available this month.

Article Title: MacKenzie Scott gives $70 million to a fund supporting Native American students; the unrestricted gift will expand tribal college scholarships, career training and a $20 million endowment under a seve
Article Text:
MacKenzie Scott gives $70 million to a fund supporting Native American students; the unrestricted gift will expand tribal college scholarships, career training and a $20 million endowment under a seven-year plan

Here’s what the American Indian College Fund said

"As the public debates the value of a higher education nationwide, in Indian Country, there is no debate. Native people know first-hand how education provides opportunities, strengthens families, provides better physical and mental health outcomes, and helps build sustainable communities. To expand the education impact in Native communities, the American Indian College Fund (College Fund) created a seven-year plan anchored by a transformative $70 million unrestricted gift from Yield Giving on behalf of Mackenzie Scott.

This gift is the second and largest investment the College Fund has received in five years from the foundation.

To create maximum impact, the College Fund first met with Native students, tribal college and university (TCU) presidents, community members, and its board of trustees, ensuring appropriate responsiveness to stakeholders’ long-term needs. Working together, they developed a thoughtful, measured strategy to create sustainable impact for generations and strengthen the College Fund’s ability to fulfill its mission.

The plan benefits students through expanded programs for TCU scholarships, college success coaching, wellness and academic resources, internships, career assessment, and mentoring. It also strengthens student pathways from college to careers, expands a family-friendly campus initiative, and strengthens culturally reflective wellness programs. Tribal colleges will enjoy increased sustainability through faculty development, expanded institutional capacity, expanded cultural and environmental programming, curriculum, research, governance training, and increased community awareness through multimedia public education and public service campaigns.

Finally, the College Fund will strengthen its long-term ability to support Native students and TCUs through visibility projects and a $20 million investment in a designated endowment.

Cheryl Crazy Bull, President and CEO of the American Indian College Fund, said, “This gift gives us more very welcome resources to build on our history of success with supporting Native students and tribal communities. We built this plan by listening first.

By pairing scholarships with culturally relevant support programs and institutions, Native students graduate and enter careers to serve their communities.

We know a teacher can change lives, and a health-care worker can save them. Both professions require a college degree. Thanks to Mackenzie Scott’s gift, we can continue building the lasting change that education provides to the well-being and prosperity of our Native communities.

We say wopila—thank you—to Mackenzie Scott for her trust in the College Fund and our mission to create stronger Native families and communities.”

Scott’s investment is being made as chronic federal and philanthropic underinvestment in Indian Country is occurring, according to a report released by the American Indian College Fund and Brookings in August, “The Underinvestment in Indian Country: How federal and philanthropic funding to Native Americans falls short, and how to fix it.”

Less than 1% of U.S. philanthropic investment serves Indian Country, while federal investments reverted to pre-pandemic levels of underfunding despite the government’s trust and treaty obligations.

Underfunding contributes to a college completion gap in Indian Country, with U.S. Census data showing currently only 16% of American Indian and Alaska Native adults have earned a bachelor’s degree or higher, compared with 33% nationally.

College Fund research shows its scholars graduate and enter careers at a rate 1.5 times higher with support beyond scholarships. Investing in students and tribal colleges is a wise public investment, with every dollar spent on TCUs netting taxpayers a $1.60 return, according to Building Local Economies of Scale: The Impact of Tribal Colleges and Universities in Rural America, a study published last year by the American Indian Higher Education Consortium.

College graduates have better economic outcomes, earn higher salaries, and communities earn greater tax revenues while spending less on assistance and health programs. Higher education is not charity but a forward-thinking investment in Native people and surrounding communities. Yet TCUs continue to be underfunded despite their strong public return.

By using Yield Giving’s investment, the College Fund will strengthen student programs and initiatives at TCUs and continue its positive impact on Native students and communities for generations to come."

Jeff Bezos’ ex-wife Mackenzie Scott has donated $70 million to the American Indian College Fund through her philanthropic organization, Yield Giving. The donations are aimed at expanding educational opportunities for Native American students. The unrestricted gift will support tribal college scholarships, career training, academic and wellness programs, and a $20 million designated endowment as part of a seven-year plan to strengthen Native students and tribal communities. “The plan benefits students through expanded programs for TCU scholarships, college success coaching, wellness and academic resources, internships, career assessment, and mentoring. It also strengthens student pathways from college to careers, expands a family-friendly campus initiative, and strengthens culturally reflective wellness programs,” the organisation said in a press release.“By using Yield Giving’s investment, the College Fund will strengthen student programs and initiatives at TCUs and continue its positive impact on Native students and communities for generations to come,” it added.
Article Summary: Mackenzie Scott gives $70 million to a fund supporting Native American students. The unrestricted gift will expand tribal college scholarships, career training and a $20 million endowment. The gift is being made as chronic federal and philanthropic underinvestment in Indian Country is occurring.

Article Title: Dario Amodei wanted OpenAI to stop taking Peter Thiel’s money over a $1.25 million campaign donation; called Thiel morally worthy of...
Article Text:
Amodei wanted Thiel’s money out of OpenAI

Amodei's Peter Thiel remarks came days after 2016 United States elections

Sam Altman stood by Thiel while Amodei wanted him out

Amodei's break from OpenAI ended with Thiel's firm backing Anthropic

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei once wanted OpenAI to stop taking money from billionaire investor Peter Thiel. The trigger was the $1.25 million Thiel gave to support Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, a move Amodei said made him “morally worthy of condemnation. ” At the time, Amodei was a few months into his job at OpenAI, where he led the safety team. He posted the remarks on the company’s internal messaging app, according to a report by The New York Times.Thiel’s money found its way to Amodei anyway, a decade later. Founders Fund, the venture capital firm Thiel co-founded, made its first direct investment in Anthropic in February this year. It co-led a $30 billion funding round that valued the company at $380 billion, and reportedly put in about $1.25 billion of its own. The firm is an OpenAI investor too, which gives it a stake in both rival labs.Three days after Trump won the US presidential election in November 2016, Amodei posted on OpenAI's internal chat that he feared the country was drifting toward authoritarianism. He also said he was uneasy doing research on militarily powerful technology in such a country, the NYT reported, citing the messages. That concern has since run through his clashes with the Pentagon over military uses of AI.Thiel was an outlier in Silicon Valley that year. The PayPal and Palantir co-founder spoke at the Republican National Convention. In October 2016 he committed his $1.25 million, split between super PACs and direct contributions to the campaign. Most of the tech industry's political money was going to Hillary Clinton.He was also tied to OpenAI from day one. When the lab was set up as a nonprofit in December 2015, Thiel was among the donors named alongside Elon Musk, Sam Altman , Reid Hoffman and Amazon Web Services. Together they pledged $1 billion.Altman's ties to Thiel ran deeper. Thiel was the largest outside investor in Hydrazine, the venture fund Altman started in 2012 after selling his first startup, Loopt. Altman has credited Thiel and Paul Graham with shaping how he invests.Thiel was a part-time partner at Y Combinator at the time, and some people called for the accelerator to drop him. Altman pushed back publicly in October 2016. "YC is not going to fire someone for supporting a major party nominee," he wrote on Twitter, now X. Weeks later, Amodei was making the opposite case inside OpenAI.Amodei didn't just want certain money out. He also helped bring other money in. In 2017, he connected OpenAI with the philanthropy run by Holden Karnofsky, where he was a technical adviser. That organisation, now called Coefficient Giving, donated $30 million to OpenAI, and Karnofsky joined its board. Karnofsky married Amodei's sister Daniela later that year.Tensions grew after Daniela joined OpenAI in 2018. That December, researcher Joshua Achiam told Altman it would be unwise to make Amodei chief ethics officer. When Achiam pushed for an outside expert, Amodei confronted him and insisted no one was better suited, people with knowledge of the discussions told the NYT.The breaking point came over GPT, the project the siblings had taken over. Amodei repeatedly told Altman he would leave if president Greg Brockman wasn't kept away from the work. Altman refused. In December 2020, the Amodeis and several colleagues quit, and Anthropic was founded four weeks later.Political money has remained a sore point. Brockman and his wife gave $25 million to MAGA Inc., the pro-Trump super PAC, in September 2025, according to federal filings reported by Bloomberg. Amodei has since called that donation "evil" in messages to colleagues, The Wall Street Journal reported earlier this year.A decade on, Amodei's views on political money have barely shifted, even as his own company's list of investors has grown more complicated. Anthropic is now preparing to go public on Nasdaq later this month.When those shares list, the firm founded by the man Amodei once wanted OpenAI to shun will sit among Anthropic's backers.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei once wanted OpenAI to stop taking money from billionaire investor Peter Thiel. The trigger was the $1.25 million Thiel gave to support Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign. Thiel's firm Founders Fund co-led a $30 billion funding round that valued the company at $380 billion.

Why UK, France and Japan renewed emergency advice

Canadian officials have reiterated their advice for Canadians to prepare to manage without essential services for at least 72 hours, after the United Kingdom, France and Japan renewed emergency preparedness calls. Public Safety Canada says the recommendation is not new and has been in place for years. The guidance asks households to be ready for disruptions to running water, electricity and basic services during emergencies. The renewed messaging comes amid concerns about severe weather, natural disasters and cyberattacks. Officials say there is no indication the international announcements are linked to an expected event, but experts say Canadians should review their supplies and plans.Public Safety Canada said the rule is not new and has been shared with residents for several years."Canadians have been encouraged for many years to ... be ready to take care of themselves and their households for a minimum of 72 hours during an emergency," Zarah Malik, a spokesperson for Public Safety Canada, said in a statement to CBC News.Suzanne Bernier, an instructor with the Disaster Recovery Institute of Canada, told CTV Your Morning on November 4 that the recommendation has been around for decades.“That message ... that we’re hearing all over around the world, and in Canada, is nothing new. It’s the exact same messaging that we’d given out ... 30 years ago,” she said.Public Safety Canada has said 72 hours is a minimum recommendation. In some areas, it may take longer to restore basic services or for emergency workers to reach residents.The UK launched its Be Ready campaign on October 22, asking people to keep essential supplies at home for three days. Officials cited risks such as cyberattacks and severe weather. Similarly, in France, authorities in Normandy urged residents on October 27 to prepare a bag with essential items for 72 hours, posting: "Don't wait for the emergency: prepare now!"Japan also launched a new national disaster management agency, with guidance asking residents to review evacuation plans and stock up on water and portable toilets for at least three days. However, there is no indication that the announcements were coordinated or linked to a specific expected emergency.Expert says Canadians should prepare for seven daysSuzanne Bernier said households should consider keeping supplies for a full week, rather than stopping at the 72-hour minimum."We're just seeing that it doesn't really matter where we are, everywhere is a target. But particularly of concern is the cyberattacks on critical infrastructure," she said. "It's just a matter of time before everybody is either indirectly or directly affected by a cyberattack," she added.
Article Summary: Canadian officials have reiterated their advice for Canadians to prepare to manage without essential services for at least 72 hours. Public Safety Canada says the recommendation is not new and has been in place for years. UK, France and Japan renewed emergency preparedness calls. Officials say there is no indication the announcements are linked to an expected event.

Article Title: 'Acid balloon' memories are back for Microsoft in Amsterdam, what's bringing the 'nightmare' back for software giant

How the attack on Microsoft unfolded

“This acidic mixture attacks concrete, and the hydrogen peroxide causes steel to rust faster,”

Why protesters are targeting the data center

“They behaved disgracefully,”

“There is a right to demonstrate in this country, and that is being completely disregarded; even the march to the data center was not facilitated.”

A group of protesters recently stormed the construction site of a massive Microsoft data center on the outskirts of Amsterdam, marking the second incident in one year where the tech giant’s AI infrastructure site has been attacked. Riot police were deployed to the scene near Sloterdijk, in Amsterdam’s western port area, and made multiple arrests.According to Dutch news agency ANP, police initially blocked the demonstration march. After Amsterdam’s mayor issued an order banning the gathering, marchers attempted to push past police lines before heading toward the construction grounds, where work is underway on a major three-building complex intended for Microsoft.Reports from local media said that roughly 100 people breached the site’s boundaries, while around 500 demonstrators entered the grounds, some remaining outside.Local news portal AN5 reported that several protesters cut or broke through perimeter fences to get in, while others climbed an on-site construction crane.Previously, the protestors filled water balloons with a mixture of hydrogen peroxide, acetic acid, salt and acrylic paint before throwing them at the facility, according to the Register.said the group in a statement at that time. Activists have also spattered the offices of fossil fuel insurers with foul-smelling butyric acid and used superglue and bicycle locks to barricade the entrance of Lloyd's, a major insurance market in London.Geef Tegengas, an advocacy group that campaigns against fossil fuels, is demanding an immediate and permanent halt to the project, arguing that it puts too much strain on local power grids. The group claims the completed facility will consume as much electricity as every household in Amsterdam combined. They warn that the massive power draw will derail the construction of 30,000 planned local homes.The development consists of three separate 85-meter-tall towers, all of which will be leased entirely by Microsoft. Initial plans for the complex were submitted in 2016—before Amsterdam enacted a municipal ban on new data center builds within the city.Meanwhile, the event’s organisers slammed the police response.they claimed.

Article Title: Microsoft sends 'China ban warning' to the US government; says: Datacenters across America will come to a grinding halt if you …
Article Text:
Microsoft sends 'China ban warning' to the US government; says: Datacenters across America will come to a grinding halt if you …

What are optical transceivers that FCC wants to ban import from China

Concerns against China-made optical transceivers

Microsoft has sent a ‘warning’ to the White House saying that data centres in the US will come to a halt if the FCC’s proposed import ban on Chinese optical transceivers is passed. According to a Reuters report, the software giant is lobbying against the move alongside the Information Technology Industry Council (ITI). Microsoft, which is building 35 data centers around the country and is planning 134 more, reportedly met the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and the National Security Council recently.“It really threatens to arguably grind (the data center rollout) to a halt,” ITI Executive Vice President of Policy and General Counsel John Miller said. “Those chips, without optical transceivers, literally could just sit there waiting around unutilized until you actually have the transceivers to essentially connect them together,” he further stated referring to the AI chips that data centers use.Optical transceivers are small devices that convert electrical signals into light signals, allowing data to travel through fibre-optic cables. Data centres increasingly use this technology to transfer data between AI chips and server racks. Compared with traditional copper cables, fibre-optic connections are faster, have lower delays, use less power and produce less heat.However, Chinese companies account for 66% of the global optical transceiver market.A ban on these companies supplying US data centres is expected to cut the available supply by more than half, worsening the shortages already affecting the industry.As stated in a Tom’s Hardware report, there are concerns that some of the optical transceivers could be compromised by Beijing which in turn can be used to steal data, install malware, or remotely disrupt American data centers. This is the likely reason why FCC is considering the ban.Notably, only two US-based companies – Coherent and Lumentum produce optical transceivers that data centers need. However, the firms don’t have the scale to make up for the shortfall if the FCC bans Chinese imports.
Article Summary: Microsoft has sent a ‘warning’ to the White House saying that data centres in the US will come to a halt if the FCC’s proposed import ban on Chinese optical transceivers is passed. The software giant is lobbying against the move alongside the Information Technology Industry Council (ITI)

Article Title: Anthropic has committed $50 million to charities in its San Francisco hometown region through 2027; its first $500,000 will support food banks, shelters, hot meals and toys for children, with more gra
Article Text:
Anthropic has committed $50 million to charities in its San Francisco hometown region through 2027; its first $500,000 will support food banks, shelters, hot meals and toys for children, with more grants planned

Which organizations will receive the first grants

Why is Anthropic investing in its hometown

How will $50 million fund work

Anthropic has committed $50 million to nonprofit organisations across the San Francisco Bay Area, with grants expected to reach local community groups by the end of 2027. The AI company said the funding will be managed through a donor advised fund at the San Francisco Foundation, with its first $500,000 being distributed immediately to four organisations. The initial grants will support food access, free community meals, winter shelter services and a toy programme for children facing difficult circumstances. The partnership focuses particularly on San Francisco, Anthropic’s hometown, where the company says it hopes to expand opportunity and strengthen local communities in the region.As announced by the company, the first $500,000 will go to four organisations supporting communities across San Francisco and nearby areas. SF-Marin Food Bank partners with 265 community organisations across two counties to help families access fresh, healthy food.GLIDE, a Tenderloin-based organisation, provides three free meals a day, 364 days a year. It also supports families as they pursue health, stable homes and opportunity. The Interfaith Winter Shelter, founded by the San Francisco Interfaith Council, has brought together more than 50 faith communities for over three decades.It provides people experiencing homelessness with a warm bed, a hot meal and a shower.San Francisco Firefighters Local 798 Toy Program, run by active and retired firefighters since 1949, provides toys to children facing difficult circumstances, including those recovering from fires or disasters, or living in family shelters, hospital wards or protective custody.San Francisco has been home to Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei since childhood. Both attended Lowell High School before starting the AI company in their hometown. Early employees also gathered at Precita Park to map out a vision for safer AI systems.Anthropic now has more than 2,500 employees at its San Francisco headquarters. Its Claude chatbot is also widely used by local businesses and nonprofits.Daniela Amodei, Co-founder and President of Anthropic, said:“San Francisco has always been a place of enormous possibility, but that possibility isn’t shared equally by everyone. We have been privileged to build Anthropic here, and we want to make sure our success expands opportunity, not widens the gaps that already exist. That’s why we’re partnering with the San Francisco Foundation, whose deep knowledge of the Bay Area will help guide this commitment to where it’s needed most,” said Daniela Amodei, Co-founder and President of Anthropic.Anthropic has established a donor advised fund at the San Francisco Foundation (SFF) to draw on the foundation’s local knowledge and direct support towards community needs. A donor advised fund is a charitable fund set aside for giving. The donor contributes money and recommends nonprofit organisations to support, while the foundation manages the details and brings its local expertise to the recommendations.SFF is a community foundation that works with donors, nonprofits and neighbours to pool resources and direct them towards regional priorities. Anthropic said it will draw on SFF’s nearly 80 years of knowledge and expertise as it determines the fund’s grant recipients.Fred Blackwell, CEO of the San Francisco Foundation, said:“Where you live matters, and so does what you put into it. The Bay Area has always been a place where people build big things. That should include building strong communities. Anthropic is making a real commitment to the place it calls home, and we hope others are inspired to do the same. That’s how the whole region thrives,” said Fred Blackwell, CEO, San Francisco Foundation.
Article Summary: Anthropic has committed $50 million to charities in its San Francisco hometown region through 2027. Its first $500,000 will support food banks, shelters, hot meals and toys for children, with more grants planned. The AI company said the funding will be managed through a donor advised fund at the San Francisco Foundation.

Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Why Jensen Huang addressed his children in the apology email

Nvidia board launches independent investigation

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s apology email to employees over his marital infidelity also contained a direct appeal to his family, including his two children who work at the AI chipmaker. Jensen Huang, who admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife, addressed the message to his colleagues at Nvidia before turning to his family and expressing hope that he could regain their trust. The email, released by Nvidia on November 8, opened with Jensen Huang saying: “I owe my family and all of you an apology.” He then wrote: “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”The message included a section addressed specifically to his wife and family. “To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust,” Huang wrote.Jensen Huang’s family has a direct connection with Nvidia’s workplace. His daughter Madison Huang and son Spencer Huang both hold roles at the company. Madison works in the Omniverse division, while Spencer is part of Nvidia’s robotics group.Madison’s husband, Nico Caprez, also works at the chipmaker and became a vice president in January.The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang has increasingly entrusted responsibilities to the next generation of his family while maintaining a hands-on leadership style at Nvidia. The company’s structure has no clear second-in-command or named successor, with Huang personally overseeing a large part of its operations.The email therefore addressed two audiences: Nvidia’s employees and board, to whom Huang apologised for falling short of his responsibilities, and his family, whose trust he said he hoped to earn back. However, Huang did not publicly explain why he chose to address his family within the company-wide message.He also made clear that he did not want his family to be held responsible for his actions. “My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy,” he wrote.The apology came amid reports that Huang had been involved in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. US intelligence officials reportedly believe Alice Huang was linked to Chinese intelligence. She is not related to Jensen Huang.Nvidia’s board announced an independent investigation into reports that its CEO had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The company said a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, would oversee the inquiry. Nvidia’s board also said it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets had been compromised, but would examine all available information.Jensen Huang said in his email that he supported the investigation and would cooperate fully. He also reaffirmed his commitment to Nvidia and to supporting US national security.The controversy has since widened. President Donald Trump said the FBI was looking into the matter and said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was allegedly involved in espionage. Nvidia and Huang have also been sued by a shareholder, who accused them of misleading investors over the alleged relationship and related national-security concerns. The claims remain allegations.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang's family has a direct connection with Nvidia’s workplace. His daughter Madison Huang and son Spencer Huang both hold roles at the company. Article Title: FDA warns against popular anti-obesity drugs; including the one Elon Musk publicly admitted taking for weight loss and said that they can improve quality of life for Americans
Article Text:
FDA warns against popular anti-obesity drugs; including the one Elon Musk publicly admitted taking for weight loss and said that they can improve quality of life for Americans

What is the condition FDA has warned about

When Elon Musk admitted taking anti-obesity drug

What FDA data says

America's Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning that popular obesity drugs, including Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound, and Mounjaro, may carry a "potential increased risk" of a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent vision loss. For those unaware, Mounjaro, Ozempic and Wegovy are all part of a buzzy class of drugs known as GLP-1 agonists, which are seen as potential game-changers for patients struggling with obesity and diabetes.In a recent drug safety communication, the FDA said that it will now require makers of GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs to add a warning about that risk on their drug labels. As per the advisory, "The US Food and Drug Administration is informing patients and health care providers of a potential increased risk of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) associated with use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) medications. NAION is a rare condition that can result in acute, painless, decreased vision in one eye, including permanent vision loss."It’s unknown how GLP-1 drugs may cause NAION. The condition is rare overall, occurring in somewhere between two and 10 people in 100,000 in the general population, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmology. These small numbers have reportedly made it more difficult to determine with certainty if there is a connection.Further complicating the potential link is the fact that the risk factors for developing NAION are common among patients taking GLP-1 drugs. The risk factors include diabetes, cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, metabolic syndrome, and obstructive sleep apnea.In December 2024, Elon Musk showed off a trimmer figure in a holiday social media post while revealing that he has been taking an anti-obesity drug to shed weight. Tesla CEO posted a photo of himself on Twitter on Christmas Day dressed up in a Santa costume, captioning the picture, "Ozempic Santa." He added, "Technically, Mounjaro, but that doesn't have the same ring to it."A few days earlier in another post on these medicines, Musk wrote, "Nothing would do more to improve the health, lifespan and quality of life for Americans than making GLP inhibitors super low cost to the public. Nothing else is even close."In July 2024, Hathaway et al. published an article titled “Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy in Patients Prescribed Semaglutide.”[1] Although FDA identified several limitations of this study, the agency determined that further assessment of the potential increased risk for NAION was warranted. Therefore, FDA undertook a comprehensive evaluation of clinical trial data, animal data, and postmarketing data, including observational studies and case reports.FDA conducted a detailed review of reports of NAION in patients treated with GLP-1 RAs that were received through the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS), formerly the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). These reports were challenging to interpret because the risk factors for NAION often overlap with conditions common in patients treated with GLP-1 RAs. Therefore, FDA evaluated other data sources, described below, to further assess for a potential relationship between GLP-1 RA use and NAION.FDA review of the available animal data did not identify a mechanism for how GLP-1 RA use could increase the potential risk of NAION.FDA performed a meta-analysis of clinical trials across GLP-1 RA development programs because of the small number or absence of cases of NAION observed in individual trials. The primary objective of the meta-analysis was to assess the incidence of NAION events in patients treated with GLP-1 RAs compared to the incidence in patients treated with a comparator (a placebo or a non-GLP-1 RA glucose-lowering medication). There were 126 such trials for GLP-1 RAs included in the meta-analysis, including a total of 134,253 patients (78,217 GLP-1 RA users and 56,036 patients receiving a comparator) with 288,879 PY of exposure (156,947 PY for the GLP-1 RA users and 131,932 PY for the patients receiving a comparator). We identified 15 probable NAION events, 10 in patients treated with GLP-1 RAs, 5 in patients receiving placebo, and none in patients who received other non-GLP-1 RA glucose-lowering medication. Overall, the results showed a NAION incidence rate of 6.4 events per 100,000 PY in patients treated with GLP-1 RAs compared to 3.8 events per 100,000 PY in comparator-treated patients.
Article Summary: Mounjaro, Ozempic and Wegovy are all part of a buzzy class of drugs known as GLP-1 agonists. FDA said it will now require makers of these drugs to add a warning on their drug labels.

Article Title: In 2025, Jensen Huang backed nepotism saying it doesn't bother him: ‘Many Nvidia second-generation employees even…’
Article Text:
Jensen Huang

A rare family presence in Silicon Valley

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recently admitted to having an extramarital affair and soon after his admission, talks surrounding succession at Nvidia have gained momentum. Amid this, an older report has resurfaced in which Huang defended nepotism during a recent company all-hands meeting, claiming that employees' children often end up doing a better job than their parents. Speaking at a recent all-hands meeting last year, Huang acknowledged that many staff members’ children work at the company and insisted it doesn't bother him. He reasoned that parents wouldn't recommend their own kids for a job if they thought they would embarrass them – and added with a smile that many “Nvidia second-generation” employees even outperform their parents.The comments come as Nvidia faces closer attention over its hiring practices, particularly because Huang’s own children, Madison and Spencer, have moved into key roles within the company’s emerging business divisions.However, Nvidia has no public succession plan and no obvious heir. Huang holds both the CEO and president titles. Under him, Nvidia has taken an estimated 90% of the market for the chips behind large Al projects. According to a report, Huang has long rejected conventional hierarchy and once said on a podcast that traditional organisational charts made no sense to him. He runs Nvidia mostly through project meetings that bring together recent graduates and senior executives in the same room.Having multiple generations under one roof is unusual for Silicon Valley, where the children of tech pioneers like Apple's Steve Jobs and Microsoft’s Bill Gates typically steered clear of their parents' companies. At Nvidia, however, the family ties extend beyond the CEO. Children of co-founder Chris Malachowsky and Director Aarti Shah also work at the firm.Rather than working in Nvidia’s core chip and data center business, Huang's children have carved out spots in newer, future-focused areas. Madison Huang leads the Omniverse department, focusing on 3D simulation and Digital Twin software. Spencer Huang concentrates on AI models and developing robotics perception software.Madison’s rapid rise at Nvidia has drawn plenty of attention across the tech industry. Just four years after joining the company, she is part of her father's core leadership team, with a 2023 compensation package that topped $1 million. Spencer, meanwhile, has taken a quieter approach, working behind the scenes on Nvidia’s robotics goals while avoiding the spotlight.Former Nvidia Vice President Greg Estes acknowledged the family connection, emphasising that both siblings “work very hard, excel in their respective fields, and have a deep attachment to the company.”
Article Summary: Jensen Huang defended nepotism during a recent company all-hands meeting. Said employees' children often end up doing a better job than their parents.
